ref_atoms.ref_content: The lc_hw_debug_en_i signal is encoded as lc_tx_t and is used through the lc_hw_debug_en_gated signal when late debug enable is enabled (through the late_debug_enable register or the otp_dis_rv_dm_late_debug_i pin). Bad values of this signal should be interpreted as 'Off', disabling debug and also memory/sba TL access. When late debug is enabled, set this to a value other than On and check: No ndmreset is possible (true because the ndmreset_ack signal is gated); No debug request can be sent to the core through debug_req_o; Instruction fetch requests through the memory window are not successful; The 'mem' and 'sba' TL interfaces are both disabled. Tests implement this with either late debug enable active (using lc_hw_debug_en_i) or inactive (using otp_dis_rv_dm_late_debug_i), with a 50% chance of each.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies lc_hw_debug_en_i signal and its gating effect on ndmreset_ack, debug_req_o, mem/sba interfaces, with clear expected behaviors.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Analogous to LC_HW_DEBUG_EN.INTERSIG.MUBI testpoint but for lc_dft_en_i when late debug enable is not active: corrupted signal is lc_dft_en_i; otherwise identical behavior (when late debug enable is off).
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Identifies lc_dft_en_i as the corrupted signal under specific condition (late debug off), inheriting the same MUBI checking behavior.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Control of whether to use late debug is governed by both the otp_dis_rv_dm_late_debug_i port and the late_debug_enable register. In both cases, bad values of the signal are interpreted as 'Off', causing debug enable to be controlled by the lc_dft_en_i port instead of the lc_hw_debug_en_i port. To test, set both the otp_dis_rv_dm_late_debug_i port and the late_debug_enable register to values that are not strict mubi true values, then check that debug enable is caused by lc_dft_en_i.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Explicitly names otp_dis_rv_dm_late_debug_i and late_debug_enable register, describes MUBI encoding interpretation and control switch to lc_dft_en_i.

ref_atoms.ref_content: There are five buffered copies of the lifecycle enable signal: LcEnFetch controls whether hart fetch requests to debug module's memory are relayed (implemented with en_ifetch_i in tlul_adapter_reg); LcEnRom controls hart access to debug module's memory, gating TL transactions; LcEnSba controls whether SBA transactions are relayed; LcEnDebugReq controls whether a debug request from the debug module is relayed to the hart; LcEnResetReq controls whether ndmreset request is relayed. These are buffered to prevent corruption of one from affecting others. Verify that when debug is disabled, forcing one copy does not activate any of the other features.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes five distinct enable copies (LcEnFetch, LcEnRom, LcEnSba, LcEnDebugReq, LcEnResetReq) with specific gating effects and buffering to avoid cross-corruption, with a verification condition.

ref_atoms.ref_content: The gate at u_tlul_lc_gate_sba has a sparse FSM; a fault injection of only a couple of bits cannot change between valid values. Inject a 1- or 2-bit error and check that the fatal_fault alert is triggered.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Points to u_tlul_lc_gate_sba gate instance, details sparse FSM behavior and the expected fatal_fault alert upon a 1-2 bit fault injection.

ref_atoms.ref_content: The gate at u_tlul_lc_gate_rom has a sparse FSM; a fault injection of only a couple of bits cannot change between valid values. Inject a 1- or 2-bit error and check that the fatal_fault alert is triggered.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Points to u_tlul_lc_gate_rom gate instance, details sparse FSM behavior and the expected fatal_fault alert upon a 1-2 bit fault injection.

ref_atoms.ref_content: The multi-bit nature of the signal is checked by all tests that disable debug (choosing an arbitrary value other than On). The rv_dm_buffered_enable test provides a tighter check that fetch requests are more tightly controlled than arbitrary TL requests.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes the multi-bit encoding check on the execution control signal and how fetch requests are more stringently controlled, verified by rv_dm_buffered_enable.
